document_info.title: DC IR-Drop Analysis of Multilayered Power Distribution Network by Discontinuous Galerkin Method With Thermal Effects Incorporated
document_info.publication: IEEE Transactions on Components, Packaging and Manufacturing Technology
document_info.core_technology: Discontinuous Galerkin Method with Electrical-Thermal Coupling

technical_overview.problem_description: DC IR-drop analysis of multilayered power distribution networks incorporating thermal effects
technical_overview.key_innovation: First successful application of Discontinuous Galerkin method for electro-thermal coupled analysis
technical_overview.main_contribution: Efficient domain decomposition method with block Thomas algorithm for large-scale problems

coupling_mechanism.electrical_to_thermal: Current generates Joule heating Q = σ|E|²
coupling_mechanism.bidirectional_coupling: Temperature → Resistivity → IR Drop → Current → Heating

domain_decomposition.concept: Divide computational domain into multiple subdomains
domain_decomposition.subdomain_arrangement: Nested sequence forming serial coupling scheme

numerical_flux.current_flux: n̂ · J̃^k = C₁₀(n̂ · J^k + n̂ · J^l) + C₁₁(n̂ · J^k - n̂ · J^l) + C₁₂(φ^k - φ^l)
numerical_flux.potential_flux: φ̃^k = C₂₀(φ^k + T^l) + C₂₁(n̂ · J^k - n̂ · J^l) + C₂₂(φ^k - φ^l)

discretization.basis_functions: Nodal basis functions for potential and current density
discretization.subdomain_matrix: M_φj^k v^k + F_φj^kl v^l + F_φφ^kk γ^k + F_φφ^kl γ^l = 0

matrix_structure.formation: Result of domain decomposition with serial coupling
matrix_structure.block_diagonal: M^k represents internal physics of subdomain k
matrix_structure.off_diagonal: F^(k,k±1) represents coupling between adjacent subdomains

block_thomas_method.lu_decomposition: A = L_B U_B where L_B is block lower triangular, U_B is block upper triangular

electro_thermal_iteration.convergence_criteria: Temperature and potential distributions reach steady state

results.with_thermal_effects: DG method results highly consistent with FEM
results.without_thermal_effects: DG method results almost coincide with analytical solution

thermal_effect_impact.observation: Thermal effects significantly influence IR drop
thermal_effect_impact.quantitative: At VDD=10V, Vdrop≈7.8V with thermal effects
thermal_effect_impact.trend: Voltage drop increases sharply with VDD when thermal effects considered

convergence_performance.convergence_curve: Relative error decreases stably with iterations
convergence_performance.voltage_dependency: Higher VDD requires more iterations but still converges

voltage_drop.distribution: Decreases from current injection point outward
voltage_drop.thermal_impact: Temperature rise causes additional voltage drop

vs_traditional_fem.matrix_scale: Local subdomain matrices vs global large matrix
vs_traditional_fem.convergence: Direct method (no convergence issues) vs iterative (uncertain convergence)
vs_traditional_fem.complex_boundaries: Natural handling via numerical flux vs difficult treatment
vs_traditional_fem.electro_thermal_coupling: Natural support vs additional processing required

core_innovations: First successful DG method for electro-thermal coupling
Domain decomposition avoiding global matrix construction
Block Thomas algorithm for efficient direct solution
Natural handling of complex geometries like 'Swiss cheese' effect

terminology.IR_Drop: Voltage drop due to current flow through resistive elements
terminology.Numerical_Flux: Approximation of physical flux at subdomain boundaries
terminology.Block_Thomas_Method: Direct solver for block tridiagonal matrix systems
terminology.Electro_Thermal_Coupling: Bidirectional interaction between electrical and thermal effects
terminology.Swiss_Cheese_Effect: Power plane with numerous vias creating hole patterns
